sections.heading: I Bring the Studio to You
sections.imageAlt: Lisa Weiss standing with her camera beside portable lights and reflectors.
sections.secondaryImageAlt: Smiling woman in a blue top photographed during a Kennewick team headshot session.
paragraphs: I don't have a studio, and for headshots that turns out to be an advantage.

I bring portable studio lighting and backdrops to wherever you work. I've photographed physicians' headshots by setting up in a clinic's lab room, and in an unused waiting area, and in a spare office nobody had touched in months. If you can give me a small corner and a little time, I can make it look like a studio.

Which means nobody on your team has to drive anywhere, block out an afternoon, or reschedule patients. That's usually the difference between a company finally updating its team page and putting it off for another year.

sections.heading: A Headshot You'll Actually Use
sections.imageAlt: Smiling woman with long blonde hair against a neutral studio backdrop.
sections.secondaryImageAlt: Smiling man wearing glasses photographed during a Kennewick team headshot session.
paragraphs: Your headshot arrives before you do. LinkedIn, your company's team page, the conference program, the proposal, the "about" page someone checks before they ever pick up the phone.
It deserves better than a cropped wedding photo or the one from three jobs ago that you keep meaning to replace.

Mine are warm and genuinely you — professional enough for the boardroom, human enough that someone feels like they've already met you. Which, in a community like the Tri-Cities, is most of the reason people call.

sections.heading: Even If You Hate Having Your Picture Taken
sections.imageAlt: Business owner seated on a black leather sofa during a West Richland branding portrait.
sections.secondaryImageAlt: Smiling man in a blue shirt photographed against a warm stone backdrop in Kennewick.
paragraphs: Most people who book headshots open with the same line: "Just so you know, I'm terrible at this."
You're not. You've just never been guided.

I'll direct the entire thing — where to put your shoulders, what to do with your hands, when to take a breath in through your nose and out through your mouth. Between prompts, the real expressions show up, and those are the ones you'll choose. The compliment I get most often in my reviews is how at ease people felt, and that includes plenty who arrived dreading it.

sections.heading: Headshots for Teams
sections.imageAlt: Smiling woman in a black top photographed during a Kennewick team headshot session.
sections.secondaryImageAlt: Smiling man wearing glasses photographed during a Kennewick team headshot session.
paragraphs: Consistent, warm headshots for your whole team, photographed on site and scheduled so it barely interrupts the workday. Tell me how many people and I'll map out the morning.
If your team page is currently a patchwork of selfies, vacation crops and photos from 2016, this is a very fixable problem — and it's usually a single visit.

sections.heading: How a Session Works
sections.imageAlt: Lisa Weiss photographing a portrait outdoors with her camera.

items.heading: Quick planning.
paragraphs: Where the headshot needs to work, what to wear, and the impression you want to give.

items.heading: I arrive and set up.
paragraphs: Portable lighting and backdrop, in whatever space you've got.

items.heading: We shoot.
paragraphs: Guided the whole way, with a few variations for options. Individuals are usually done well within the hour.

items.heading: You choose.
paragraphs: A gallery of edited images, retouched honestly — I'll take care of the temporary things and leave you looking like you.

sections.heading: Headshot Questions
sections.imageAlt: Business professional holding a coffee cup during a relaxed Richland branding portrait.

items.heading: Do you have a studio?
paragraphs: No — I bring one to you. Portable studio lighting and backdrops set up at your office, clinic or workplace anywhere in the Tri-Cities.

items.heading: What should I wear for a headshot?
paragraphs: Solid colors near your face photograph best. Avoid busy patterns and large logos. Bring two or three options and I'll help you choose when I arrive.

items.heading: How long does a headshot session take?
paragraphs: Usually under an hour for an individual. Team sessions depend on headcount — most teams are done in a morning.

items.heading: Do you retouch headshots?
paragraphs: Gently and honestly. A blemish, a stray hair, a collar sitting oddly. What I won't do is smooth you into someone else — you should still look like you on a very good day.

items.heading: Do I need a headshot or a branding session?
paragraphs: If you need one great portrait, a headshot. If you need a library of images of you, your work and your space, that's branding.

items.heading: Can you photograph our whole team in one visit?
paragraphs: Yes, and that's usually how it's done. Send me a headcount and I'll build a schedule around your workday.

finalCta.heading: Let's Update That Profile Photo
paragraphs: Tell me where your headshot needs to work and when you need it.
